passage:
Outside the train station, there is a wooden box filled with books. A sign says, "Take a book. Leave a book."
No one watches the box all day, but it stays full. Some books are children's stories. Others are novels, cookbooks, or travel guides.
A woman once took a book because her train was delayed. She finished half of it during the trip and returned it the next week with another book.
The box works because people trust strangers they may never meet.
It is not a library, and there are no due dates. Still, many people treat it carefully. The free book box reminds the town that sharing can happen quietly in public places.
